meta.storyTitle: Replace chain.ts's dead CLI next-step commands and docs/workflow.md's dead amendment CLI with the real MCP mechanism

summary.prose: Fixes two surfaces that still tell an agent (or a human reading docs/workflow.md) to run `insrc workflow approve/amend/sync ...` -- CLI commands that do not exist. src/workflow/chain.ts's computeNextAction() swaps those dead strings for the real insrc_workflow_approve({artifactPath}) / insrc_workflow_step(phase='start', workflow='tracker.sync', ...) call shapes already used by every other case in the same function. For review-amendment specifically, buildChainReport now looks up the first pending amendment's real id/path (reusing listAmendments + amendmentPath, already imported) and passes it through as a new internal-only field so the case can finally name a real artifact instead of an invented list command. docs/workflow.md's two amendment sections are rewritten to show the real mechanism instead.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Replace chain.ts's dead CLI next-step commands and docs/workflow.md's dead amendment CLI with the real MCP mechanism

dataModelChanges.details: Add `firstPendingAmendment: { readonly id: string; readonly path: string } | undefined`, computed in buildChainReport by filtering listAmendments(repoPath, epicHash) to status==='pending' (keeping listAmendments's existing deterministic AMD-<hash>-<n> order) and taking the first, mapped via amendmentPath(repoPath, id). ChainReport.amendments (the public counts-only field) and countAmendments() are both left exactly as they are -- this is an additional, separate input to computeNextAction, not a change to the existing one.

The TYPE shape of the 'review-amendment' member (`{ kind: 'review-amendment'; amendmentId: string; command: string }`) does not change. Only its runtime VALUE changes: amendmentId becomes the real AMD-<epicHash>-<n> id (or a fallback literal when, in a theoretically-impossible race, no pending row is found despite s.amendments.pending > 0) instead of the placeholder '<list via: ...>' string, and command becomes a real, runnable instruction naming insrc_present + insrc_workflow_approve instead of the dead 'insrc workflow amend ... --list' string.

The documented CLI examples change from the invented `insrc workflow amend <h16> --list/--show/--approve/--reject` to the real mechanism: discovering a pending AMD-<epicHash>-<n> artifact, then insrc_present({documents:[path]}) followed by insrc_workflow_approve({artifactPath: path}). Surrounding prose describing the AMD lifecycle itself (pending/approved/rejected) is unchanged.

errorCases.scenario: The pending amendment counted by countAmendments gets approved or rejected by a concurrent session between buildChainReport's countAmendments call and its new listAmendments-filtered-to-pending lookup, so amendments.pending > 0 but firstPendingAmendment comes back undefined.
errorCases.detection: firstPendingAmendment is undefined while s.amendments.pending > 0 inside computeNextAction's review-amendment branch.
errorCases.response: Do not throw. Fall back to a safe, clearly-labelled placeholder command (e.g. naming the epicHash and instructing a re-check) rather than crashing buildChainReport or returning a stale/wrong amendmentId -- this is a report-generation helper, not a mutating action, so a graceful 'recompute' fallback is always safe.
errorCases.userImpact: The chain report shows a slightly less specific next-action for one report call; the next buildChainReport call (always re-read from disk, no caching) picks up the now-current amendment state correctly.

edgeCases.input: Multiple amendments are pending simultaneously under the same epicHash.
edgeCases.expected: review-amendment names only the FIRST pending amendment in listAmendments's existing deterministic AMD-<hash>-<n> ascending order -- consistent with every other NextAction case that walks s.stories and returns on the FIRST match (e.g. the existing stale/missing-LLD loop at chain.ts:403-424).

edgeCases.input: No amendments exist at all for the epicHash (s.amendments.pending === 0).
edgeCases.expected: The review-amendment branch is never entered; behavior is unchanged from today.

invariantsToPreserve.text: computeNextAction stays a pure, synchronous function of its precomputed NextActionInput -- no filesystem I/O moves into the decision function itself; all data (including the new firstPendingAmendment) is precomputed by buildChainReport, matching every existing field (define/hld/stories/amendments/tracker).
Every NextAction kind's command string that is ALREADY correct (run-define, run-hld, run-lld, push-tracker) is left byte-for-byte unchanged -- only the 7 identified dead-string sites are touched.
ChainReport.amendments's public shape ({pending, approved, rejected} counts) and countAmendments()'s return type are both left completely unchanged.

testLevels.purpose: Assert computeNextAction()/buildChainReport() return the real MCP call shape for every previously-dead NextAction kind, and that review-amendment names a real amendment id/path, while every unrelated kind's existing command string and every existing test's assertion (e.g. chain-issue-anchored.test.ts:225's `.command.includes('DEF.md')`) keeps passing unchanged.
fixturesNeeded: a pending AMD-<epicHash>-1 artifact written via the existing amendments/store.ts helpers for the review-amendment case

provingTests: src/workflow/__tests__/chain.test.ts: approve-define/approve-hld/approve-lld return a command string of the form insrc_workflow_approve({artifactPath:"<real path>"}) that still includes the real artifact path (keeping chain-issue-anchored.test.ts:225's existing `.includes('DEF.md')` assertion passing)
src/workflow/__tests__/chain.test.ts: sync-tracker returns an insrc_workflow_step phase=start workflow=tracker.sync command naming the real epicHash

src/workflow/__tests__/chain.test.ts: with one pending AMD artifact present, review-amendment's amendmentId equals that artifact's real id and command names its real path via insrc_present + insrc_workflow_approve
src/workflow/__tests__/chain.test.ts: with two pending AMD artifacts present, review-amendment names the FIRST in AMD-<hash>-<n> ascending order
A new assertion (or manual inspection, since docs/workflow.md has no existing test harness) confirming docs/workflow.md's two amendment sections no longer contain the string 'insrc workflow amend'

testStrategy.testFramework: node:test (via tsx), matching every existing test in src/workflow/__tests__/

migration.stateBefore: Per the s1 analyze bundles: 7 of computeNextAction()'s return sites (src/workflow/chain.ts, cited lines) emit an invented CLI string ('insrc workflow approve/amend/sync ...') as the NextAction's command/amendmentId; NextActionInput carries only count-based amendments data with no per-amendment identifier; docs/workflow.md's two amendment sections document the same invented CLI.
migration.stateAfter: The same 7 sites emit the real insrc_workflow_approve({artifactPath}) / insrc_workflow_step(phase='start', workflow='tracker.sync', ...) call shapes; NextActionInput additionally carries a precomputed firstPendingAmendment {id, path} (ChainReport.amendments's own public shape unchanged); docs/workflow.md's two sections show the real present+approve mechanism instead.

migrationSteps.action: In buildChainReport, compute firstPendingAmendment from listAmendments(repoPath, epicHash) filtered to status==='pending' (first in existing order), mapped via amendmentPath; add it to the NextActionInput object alongside the existing define/hld/stories/amendments/tracker fields.

In computeNextAction, replace the 6 approve-*/sync-tracker dead-string return sites with the real insrc_workflow_approve({artifactPath}) / insrc_workflow_step(...) call-shape strings, keeping each site's existing real path/epicHash embedded in the string (preserving existing test assertions like .command.includes('DEF.md')).

In computeNextAction's review-amendment branch, use the new firstPendingAmendment input (when present) to return the real amendmentId and a command naming insrc_present + insrc_workflow_approve with that real path; fall back to a non-throwing placeholder only in the error-paths race case.
Update docs/workflow.md's two amendment sections' code examples to the real mechanism, leaving the surrounding AMD-lifecycle prose unchanged.

Update/extend src/workflow/__tests__/chain.test.ts (and confirm chain-issue-anchored.test.ts's existing assertions still pass unmodified) to assert the new real command content for the 7 corrected sites.

migration.backwardCompat: No public API/type signature changes: NextAction's exported type shape is unchanged (only runtime string VALUES change for the 7 sites); NextActionInput is internal/unexported so its new field is not a breaking change for any external caller; ChainReport.amendments's public shape is completely untouched. No persisted data format changes -- this is pure in-memory report-generation + static doc content.

alternativesConsidered.name: Additive internal-only pending-amendment input
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: buildChainReport derives the first pending amendment's real {id, path} via listAmendments and passes it to computeNextAction as a new field, without touching ChainReport.amendments's existing counts-only public shape.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add a new field (e.g. `firstPendingAmendment: { id: string; path: string } | undefined`) to NextActionInput, computed in buildChainReport by filtering listAmendments(repoPath, epicHash) to status==='pending' and taking the first in its existing deterministic AMD-<hash>-<n> order, mapping to {id, path: amendmentPath(repoPath, id)}. review-amendment then returns the real amendmentId and a command string naming the real present+approve mechanism. computeNextAction stays a pure function of precomputed inputs, matching every other NextActionInput field (define/hld/stories/amendments/tracker are all already precomputed this way) -- no I/O moves into the decision function.
pros: ChainReport.amendments's public shape (pending/approved/rejected counts) is completely unchanged, so any existing renderer/test reading those three numbers is unaffected
computeNextAction remains pure/deterministic given its inputs, consistent with the existing convention
listAmendments and amendmentPath already exist and are already imported into chain.ts -- pure reuse, no new store-layer code
cons: NextActionInput gains one more field; a caller constructing it by hand (if any exists outside buildChainReport) would need updating too

alternativesConsidered.name: Expand ChainReport.amendments's public shape to carry pending identifiers
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Change ChainReport.amendments from {pending,approved,rejected} counts to also include a `pendingList: {id,path}[]` array, surfacing it as part of the report's own public contract rather than as an internal-only input.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Widen the ChainReport.amendments type and countAmendments's return value to also carry the pending rows' real ids/paths (not just counts), then have computeNextAction read from that same field instead of a separate internal-only one.
pros: Every consumer of ChainReport (not just computeNextAction) also gets the real pending-amendment identifiers for free, e.g. for a richer chain-report rendering later
cons: Changes a PUBLIC, already-consumed artifact shape (ChainReport.amendments) for a need only computeNextAction currently has -- larger blast radius for no immediate consumer

Any existing test asserting ChainReport.amendments's exact shape (e.g. a deepEqual against {pending,approved,rejected}) breaks and needs updating even though its own concern (the counts) didn't change
Speculative: no other caller needs this yet, violates 'don't add flexibility nobody asked for'
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Achieves the same functional result as a1 but widens ChainReport.amendments's public, already-consumed shape for a need only computeNextAction has today, forcing unnecessary test churn.

alternativesConsidered.name: No data-flow change; generic rediscovery instruction
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Leave ChainReport.amendments and computeNextAction's inputs exactly as they are; review-amendment's command names only the real approval mechanism in the abstract, without a specific amendment id.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Replace the dead 'insrc workflow amend ... --list' string with a generic instruction such as 'present each pending AMD-<epicHash>-* artifact under .insrc/artifacts, then insrc_workflow_approve({artifactPath})', with amendmentId left as a placeholder note rather than a real id -- zero changes to NextActionInput or ChainReport.amendments.
pros: Smallest possible diff: only the string literals change, no type/shape change at all
Zero risk of breaking any existing shape-asserting test
cons: Doesn't actually fix the underlying gap the ISSUE's rootCause named (review-amendment still can't name a real artifact, just describes how to find one) -- less useful to an agent driving the chain than a1's real id/path
The 'exact next command' contract every sibling case honors (a real, directly-runnable call) is only partially restored for this one kind
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Cheapest, but leaves review-amendment unable to name a real artifact -- the actual defect the ISSUE's rootCause identified remains unfixed.
